prompt: Create a visual direction for a cross-platform desktop editor whose interaction model is already approved. It must feel at home on macOS and Windows while retaining one product identity; users work in long sessions with dense sidebars, search results, diagnostics, and a central canvas; light and dark appearances are required; window sizes vary widely; long localized labels and large text must remain usable. Produce the visual system and verification matrix without redesigning workflows or inventing product content.

requirements: current desktop screenshots and platform constraints

falsifiableChecks.assertion: The direction identifies which visual decisions express shared product identity and which adapt to macOS/Windows conventions, with evidence-based rationale rather than making both platforms visually identical by default.
Typography, spacing, color, iconography, emphasis, density, and light/dark appearance form a reusable system tied to supplied assets/content instead of a one-screen decoration.
Representative dense/sparse, focus, selection, diagnostic, long/localized text, large-text, and supported window-size states remain legible and hierarchically coherent.
Where motion is introduced, its informational purpose and reduced-motion behavior are explicit; critical state is not conveyed only through animation or color.

The artifact changes visual treatment only, preserves the approved interaction/content contracts, and defines verification in representative native/rendered states rather than claiming quality from a single ideal screenshot.

evidence: shared identity versus platform convention rationale
reduced-motion handling where motion is used
